BEGINNER1. Actionability Checks

Before performing virtually any action, Playwright automatically verifies the target element is:

  • Attached — present in the DOM
  • Visible — has non-zero size and no display: none/visibility: hidden
  • Stable — not mid-animation, same position across two consecutive frames
  • Enabled — not disabled
  • Receiving events — not obscured by another element on top of it

These checks run silently and repeatedly (with short retries) before every click(), fill(), check(), and similar methods — this is what eliminates most race-condition flakiness without you writing manual waits.

What this replaces: in older tools you'd write waitForElementVisible(), then waitForElementEnabled(), then finally click. Playwright folds all of that into the action call itself.

BEGINNER2. Clicking

await locator.click();
await locator.dblclick();
await locator.click({ button: 'right' });           // context menu
await locator.click({ modifiers: ['Control'] });   // Ctrl+Click
await locator.click({ modifiers: ['Shift'] });     // Shift+Click
await locator.click({ position: { x: 50, y: 30 } }); // click a specific pixel offset
await locator.click({ timeout: 10_000 });          // per-action timeout

Right-Click Context Menu Example

await page.getByTestId('file-item').click({ button: 'right' });
await page.getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Rename' }).click();

BEGINNER3. Text Input: fill() vs pressSequentially()

Method How it works When to use
fill(text) Clears the field and sets the value atomically (like a paste) The default choice — fast and reliable for nearly all forms
pressSequentially(text, opts) Simulates real key-down/key-up events for each character Autocomplete widgets or custom key-event listeners that fill() bypasses 
await locator.fill('user@example.com');    // instant, atomic
await locator.clear();                     // clear only, no new value

await locator.pressSequentially('playwright', { delay: 50 }); // key-by-key, 50ms apart
⚠️ Common Pitfall: Reaching for pressSequentially() everywhere "to be safe" makes the suite noticeably slower for no benefit on ordinary inputs. Use it only when a test specifically needs to trigger per-keystroke behavior like a live search dropdown.

INTERMEDIATE4. Keyboard Actions

await locator.press('Enter');
await locator.press('Control+A');
await locator.press('Tab');
await locator.press('ArrowDown');

// Global keyboard (not tied to a specific locator)
await page.keyboard.press('Control+A');
await page.keyboard.type('Playwright');

Autocomplete Selection Example

test('keyboard-driven search selection', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  await page.getByPlaceholder('Search').pressSequentially('play', { delay: 80 });
  await page.getByPlaceholder('Search').press('ArrowDown');
  await page.getByPlaceholder('Search').press('Enter');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('result-count')).not.toBeEmpty();
});

INTERMEDIATE5. Form Controls: Checkboxes and Selects

await page.getByLabel('Terms').check();
await page.getByLabel('Newsletter').uncheck();

await page.getByLabel('Country').selectOption('US');                     // by value
await page.getByLabel('Country').selectOption({ label: 'United States' }); // by visible label
await page.getByLabel('Country').selectOption({ index: 0 });             // by position
await page.getByLabel('Skills').selectOption(['js', 'ts']);              // multi-select

Full Registration Form

test('register a new account', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/register');

  await page.getByLabel('Full name').fill('Alice Smith');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('alice@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Secure#1234');

  await page.getByLabel('I agree to the Terms of Service').check();
  await page.getByLabel('Country').selectOption({ label: 'United States' });

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Create account' }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/welcome');
});
💡 Tip: check() is idempotent — calling it on an already-checked checkbox is a no-op rather than toggling it off. This is safer than click() for checkboxes because you never accidentally flip the state in the wrong direction.

INTERMEDIATE6. Mouse Actions: Hover, Drag, Scroll

await locator.hover();                                          // reveal tooltips/menus
await page.locator('#src').dragTo(page.locator('#dst'));       // drag and drop
await page.mouse.wheel(0, 300);                                 // scroll down 300px

Hover to Reveal a Tooltip

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Info' }).hover();
await expect(page.getByRole('tooltip')).toBeVisible();

ADVANCED7. File Uploads

await page.getByLabel('Upload').setInputFiles('report.pdf');
await page.getByLabel('Upload').setInputFiles(['a.pdf', 'b.pdf']); // multiple files
await page.getByLabel('Upload').setInputFiles([]);                 // clear selection
test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/files');
  await page.getByLabel('Choose file').setInputFiles('report.pdf');
  await expect(page.getByText('report.pdf')).toBeVisible();
});
No native file dialog needed: setInputFiles() sets the file directly on the <input type="file"> element programmatically, bypassing the OS-native file picker dialog that Playwright cannot otherwise interact with.

ADVANCED8. Overriding Auto-Waiting

await locator.click({ force: true });   // skip actionability checks
await locator.click({ trial: true });   // dry-run: check readiness, don't actually click
⚠️ Common Pitfall: { force: true } should be a deliberate, rare exception — for example, clicking an element deliberately covered by a custom overlay you know is safe to ignore. Reaching for it as a default fix for "element not clickable" errors usually just masks a real timing bug or a genuinely broken UI state that real users would also struggle with.

ADVANCED9. Common Pitfalls

⚠️ Pitfall 1 — Clicking a label instead of its input: Sometimes it's more robust to interact with the labelled control via getByLabel() directly rather than clicking visible text near it, especially on custom-styled checkboxes/radios where the visual element and the real <input> are not the same node.
⚠️ Pitfall 2 — Not waiting for the result of an action: An action completing doesn't guarantee the UI has finished reacting to it. Always follow a click that triggers async work with an expect() assertion on the expected outcome, rather than assuming the next line is safe to run immediately.

📋 Quick Reference Summary

Concept Key Points
Actionability Attached, visible, stable, enabled, receiving events — checked automatically before every action.
fill() vs pressSequentially() fill() = atomic set (default); pressSequentially() = real per-key events (autocomplete).
press() Single key or shortcut, e.g. 'Enter', 'Control+A', 'ArrowDown'.
check()/uncheck() Idempotent checkbox control; selectOption() for dropdowns.
Mouse hover(), dragTo(), page.mouse.wheel() for scrolling.
File upload setInputFiles(path) sets files directly — no OS dialog interaction needed.
{ force: true } Skips actionability checks — use sparingly and deliberately.
